text.p: Embattled Canadian 88 Energy Corp, in the wake of a cease-trade order issued by securities regulators, said on Friday it would extend its offer for Morrison Petroleums Ltd until February 19.
Canadian 88 said it extended its C$652-million bid to accommodate a hearing before the Ontario and Alberta securities commissions sheduled for Monday.

The regulators were expected to determine whether all Morrison stockholders should be given the opportunity to sell their shares to Canadian 88 on at least the same cash terms as those afforded associated West Central Capital Corp on the days leading up to the offer announcement.
Canadian 88 also said it provided the regulatory bodies with "additional disclosure" regarding questions over its bid and relationship with West Central.
The company also said regulators had reviewed the new documents.

Company chief executive Greg Noval repeated in a statement that his firm had no intention of extending the offer, but the hearing and halt of trading in shares related to the bid left it with no choice.

"Canadian 88 believes it has addressed fully and completely the concerns regarding disclosure and I welcome the opportunity to return to a debate on the merits of our offer," Noval said. "This additional disclosure plus a resolution of the pre-bid integration issue on Monday will allow the market and Morrison shareholders to focus on our offer and its potential."
The cash and share-swap deal was to have expired today.
